newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda sees $3.5 million loss from coffee disease.
newsitem.headline: Uganda sees $3.5 million loss from coffee disease.

text.p: The Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said on Tuesday coffee wilt disease sweeping across the country would cost $3.5 million in the next two to five years.

A report by the UCDA, the industry's top policy body, said the economic implication of such a loss from tracheomycosis would be profound in the growing districts of Luwero, Kibogo, Mubende, Kibaale, Masindi Mpigi and Hoima.
The report recommended that movements of unprocessed coffee be restricted and affected coffee trees destroyed.
The coffee wilt disease is a fungal infection attacking the roots of the tree. UCDA has spent $200,000 in educating farmers about the disease.
Researchers say infected coffee plants must be uprooted and burned.
